After beating about half of the game, I realized that there were some "insanity" levels on top of the baseline difficulty which boosts enemies even further and gives stronger rewards. You can tweak this at will. Treat this game and its difficulty philosophy as if it was an ARPG (which in essence it kind of is) and if you're not as stubborn as I was, do yourself a favor and boost your starting character on something a bit lower and then switch the difficulties upwards when you feel like it's time. 

All in all, this is an extremely satisfying game with beautiful visuals which will keep you hooked for a long time. If you are looking to mindlessly slay all sorts of robotic and demonic creatures with myriad satisfying weapons, this is it. Oh, and if you don't like guns much, it is completely viable to build into a melee play style entirely.  

Best 3 bucks I have EVER spent by far.

Words cannot describe what a WIERD trip Shadow Warrior as a franchise is:
1. The first game's a classic Build Engine shooter.
2. The reboot is a linear hack and slash/shooter hybrid that has its dull moments but can also be really bloody awesome.
2.5 I KID YOU NOT, there is an entire game's worth of story taking place between the reboot and the sequel, that barely gets a few mentions at best (and I would argue that would have been a very interesting tale at that).  
3. Shadow warrior 2 is in a sense a Hack and Slash Borderlands with coop and some of THE MOST satisfying and visceral first person melee combat I have ever seen. 
3.5 Bloody hell, ANOTHER game's worth of story takes place.
4. Shadow Warrior 3 is a semi-reboot, high quality movement shooter that sheds almost the entirety of its original identity, yet STILL tries to put the entire reboot franchise's plot. Gone is the incredibly visceral swordplay (though there is a sword still present here, I would say it kinda takes a more support role, than the spotlight it needs), gone is the custom visual charm of their in house engine (as the game switched to unreal). Shadow Warrior 3 is a good, no, a VERY good game, and I absolutely loved playing through it from the start to the very finish, but it's not a Shadow Warrior game. 

The only thing I can say is - Go play these games, they are not perfect.
But fuck me, if they are not fun.

I loved the first game, but I'm not impressed with this second iteration, even though it is much prettier. I'll try to explain why. 

The first Shadow Warrior game was an arcade style shooter with fancy sword fights, cool magical powers, and a pretty cliche, yet funny story, which developed logically. The main characters had some pretty good back and forth going most of the time, and Wang's one liners were usually lame, but funny.

Shadow Warrior 2 just ... [b][i]tries too hard[/i][/b]. 

First of all, the game feels like a Borderlands clone, with strong influences from the MMO genre. You teleport to different areas willy nilly, fight constantly respawning monsters, and generally manage your inventory trying to find the best gear possible (weapons and upgrades). Also gone are most of your previous magical powers, which is BS to say the least. Sword fighting is now much more one-dimensional, and less refined. You hack away at enemies rather than suspending a bunch of them in the air with your abilities, and sending a single energy wave through them, killing them all.

There's also a main "town" that you always return to, where you pick up new quests, which are marked with an exclamation mark on your minimap. Totally in the spirit of Shadow Warrior, and not, say, WoW, right? Oh, wait.

But I could almost live with all this if it weren't for the fact that the heart and soul of the game are just ... dead. Wang was always straddling the line between bad-a$$ one liners, and lame comments. But now? He's always trying to be super cocky, usually to the detriment of the character. 

Following the second mission, Wang becomes host to a second soul through a very contrived reason. The story feels so forced and weird that it manages - in only the first couple of hours - to make the first game seem a masterpiece by comparison. And this is where things really go down hill.

The soul you are burdened with belongs to the daughter of the Yakuza boss. She is some sort of genius who had infiltrated Zilla's corporation, and became his protege, but is caught spying, and punished by being injected with a poison which opens her up to demonic possession or something. And she is a grade-A, entitled, queen-bee, mean-girls-villain type b!tch.

Literally every other word out of her mough is a patronizing line about Wang being a brain-dead, over-muscled, insert-expletive-here loser, usually uttered in a hysterial, near scream. For example:

[b]Character:[/b] Do you have my item?
[b]Her(in your head):[/b] Give him the item!
[b]Wang:[/b] Your contact was dead.
[b]Character:[/b] That's a shame. So the item is lost?
[b]Her(in your head):[/b] Just give him the f***ing item, you !d!ot!
[b]Wang:[/b] The trail was not completely dead.
[b]Her(in your head):[/b] Give him the item!!! GAHHHH! *insert incoherent screams of rage and frustration here as the conversation continues*

The Yakuza second in command is also a raging b!tch who calls Wang a [b]"useless sack of sh!t"[/b] -among other terms of endearment - for no discernable reason except to emphasize that she's in charge, and he's the scum she gets to walk all over. For example, she'll send Wang after some drug manufacturing competitors in order to "send a message". Seems pretty clear that she wants them dead. He kills them, then she chews him out for having followed her vague, shadowy instructions: 

[b][i]"You dumb piece of sh!t, I told you to send a message, not kill them. You're so f-ing stup!d! You f-ing mor0n! You piece of ... !"[/i][/b]. It goes on for a while.

I simply do not understand what the developers though this kind of cr@p would add to the game, other than a compelling reason to stop playing it. Is this their twisted idea of what strong female characters should be like? Jesus. 

In the first game [b][i]Wang was a bad-a$$[/i][/b], what the heck happened here? The assassin twins showed him a certain measure of respect, and even Zilla acknowledged that Wang is supremely competent. Now we have to endure these sort of insulting diatribes all the f***ing time, and I, for one, just can't stomach it. 

Wang, the man who took sh!t from [i]no one[/i] in the first game, simply let's these chicks walk all over him as if it were cool. This, more than anything, kills any connection I might have felt for the game.

This game was just so addictive and satisfying. It just has the perfect blend of FPS and hack & slash. With an huge variety of weapons to choose from, you can practically customise how you play the game. Moreover, you get different upgrades for your weapons, so every weapon would be different. The graphics and effects were high tier as well. This game is moderately different from Shadow Warrior 1, with its open world elements, it feels even better. Shadow Warrior 1's story was still better than this though, but this game definitely stands its ground. Definitely recommended.

Genuinely the best $3 I’ve ever spent in my life.

When I bought this game, I became unbelievably addicted. I’ve always been a PvP kind of guy, not really into story games. I like action. I like adrenaline. The story here is relatively funny the first time through, but if you’re like me and enjoy the combat as much as I do, you’ll be replaying it on higher and higher difficulties anyway. Luckily, you can skip the cutscenes.

When you increase the difficulty, enemies spawn more frequently, they get bigger, and they gain new elemental resistances. The maps are semi-procedurally generated, which I actually love and wish there was even more of.

I’d recommend spending 20 minutes just messing with the settings and really learning the movement. Get used to spamming dash. That’s where the peak is. This game is all about the swords. The sword combat is on another level. The guns feel weaker by comparison. You can run gun builds, but when it comes to the peak experience, this is a sword game.

I’m currently running Insanity 3. The fun has started to taper off a bit for me, but I’ve gotten well over 100 hours out of it and was discovering new weapons almost the entire time. There are over 70 weapons. Not all are completely unique, but most have distinct perks that encourage different builds. It’s impossible to get everything in one playthrough.

I don’t think you’ve truly experienced the game until you’ve played on Insanity. That doesn’t mean start there. Play Normal first, collect weapons, build your character, then carry that progress into higher difficulties.

You can fully upgrade all the cards in the game, but it takes a long time. There are real stakes. When you die, your experience level resets. If you’re one kill away from leveling up and you die, it’s gone. You also lose a slice of your money, and money matters. Once you unlock the Forge, you’ll burn through cash fast rerolling perks.

If you want to cheat a little, switch to Insanity 7 before using the Forge for better rolls, then switch back. It doesn’t really matter though. The game is about finding that balance between too easy and too hard. When you find it, it’s some of the most intense PvE gameplay I’ve ever experienced.

It’s co-op, but none of your friends will understand how peak this game is. Accept that it’s a solo quest and carry on, fellow wizard.

And yes, Shadow Warrior 3 is a completely different game. It feels like a wacky version of Doom. They slowed the pacing and made it super short. I wish they’d taken what worked here and expanded it instead.

This game has all the pieces to be something insane. Infinite mode. Mod support. Custom maps. It could have become one of the best MMO-RPG hybrids ever made. The foundation is there. The devs clearly had fun. It was successful. I don’t understand why they changed direction.

Are the models great? Not really. Animations are mid. Story is mid. Jokes are fine.
Combat is peak.
Enemy designs are peak.

Hitboxes can be a little wonky. You’ll get stuck on a rock sometimes. But if you want the fastest sword play on the market, this is it. Infinite dashes. You can practically fly halfway across the map. I’m honestly surprised there aren’t more speedruns.

I genuinely cannot find another game that hits like this one does. Maybe dash sword Light in The Finals comes close, but that’s PvP and not the same.

My only real issue is that there isn’t more of it. I want it to be infinite.

In a way, it kind of is. After Insanity 7, you can add co-op scaling up to four players. Enemies scale with each added player, so it almost feels like 21 difficulty levels. But eventually they stop adding more enemies or making them bigger. They just get spongier.

Would I recommend it? It targets a very specific type of gamer. I know I’m that type. You’ll replay the same quests and they’ll feel different until eventually they don’t. After 100 plus hours, collecting every weapon and grinding alone, you might burn out.

But for $3, that’s less than a coffee.

Check it out. And maybe email the devs asking them to make Shadow Warrior 4 more like Shadow Warrior 2, because this was a genuinely unique experience in my gaming life. I’ll never forget it.

For me personally, I can’t fully express the level of fun I’ve gotten from this game.

Maybe you won’t love it the same way. but id at least check it out. Try to push past the wonk, learn ton control the wonk. Most of all, put on some crazy music and lock tf in, this one is a wild addiction if it hits for you.

Shadow Warrior has quickly become one of my favorite games. I'm not sure I have words enough to describe this beauty. 
But I'll try to sum it up: 

[b]+ Huge weapon collection[/b]
           (From katanas, to ninjastars, to shotguns, to chainsaws, They kind of had it all!)
[b]+ Great upgrade system[/b]
           (You get three slots on your weapons, and you can put in gems and remove whenever you feel like it)
           (Later in the game, you can make this four slots)
           (There is a forge where you can put in three upgrades, and get one higher level upgrade back. Made farming for money a lot of fun)
[b]+ Skill reset at the store[/b]
          (Speaking of skill reset, there were skill-cards you could get. Which could do a number of things: Increase HP, increase loot-radius, and even give your weapons special attacks. You'd get skill points when leveling, and this could be used on these cards.)

[b]+ The game has an amazing photo-mode[/b], normally I'll thank the gods when any game has an Hide-UI option, because I like screenshots. SW2 takes this to the extreme, in photo-mode you freeze everything, you can move the camera around and even change settings (and add filter. As I said: to the extreme!) Sadly this doesn't work in multiplayer mode. 

[b]+ A lot of difficulty settings.[/b]
Personally, I don't consider myself the most skilled gamer so I'm quite surprised that me and my partner finished this game on the forth difficulty settings (insanity). We had started the game on normal, changed to hard after two hours. And at the 6 hour-mark I found it too easy, and started fresh on insanity mode. Now this might be because we were multiplayer, and multiplayer might have balance issues but even insanity was easy at times. Of course, once you beat the game you unlock insanity 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7. Depending on your level of course. We tried insanity 3 and it was super hard, we'd have to change out all our weapon gems and tactics or we couldn't do it. 
(I of course decided to start insanity mode on fresh, because if I was gonna finish it on insanity, I was darn well gonna get the achievement for it! Which you don't get if you change your difficulty in the middle of the game. Funnily the hardest part of insanity was the tutorial mission, because you had no upgrades to play with and only two weapons)
(Found out later though, that I could have started a new game with the previous character and changed the difficulty level)


[b]Multiplayer:[/b]
+ Can change difficulty depending on how many players you are, (aka: not forced into a 4 man party and so on, you can be 2, 3, 5, etc etc)
- The host had to connect to a map before the others could, which includes clicking a button at the end of the loading screen. Which means if the host takes a quick brb, the others won't be able to enter the map untill the host returns. 
- Some multiplayer achievements are bugged if you're not the host. (Mostly story-related achievements, but a few other random ones)
- As the host of the game, I got more information. Like, when hitting a mob I'd get an arrow up or down next to my damage that would tell me if my elemental damage was being resisted or not, my partner didn't get these arrows. 
- Photo-mode doesn't work in multiplayer, not even in the main town or in places where there were no mobs. 


[b]Last notes:[/b]
As a warning, I'd like to note that there is a lot of swearing and mature language in the game. (and quite a lot of immature jokes). Personally I found the characters hilarious and fell completely inlove with Lo Wang. 

The game is beautiful, the story had a few twists I wasn't expecting, the combat is sleek, it's one of those must-plays if you're a co-oper.

Definitely one of the best FPS games to play, it really makes you feel like a katana-wielding badass. Honestly 50% of the time I have no idea what's happening because enemies keep spawning around me keep attacking with ludicrous amounts of projectiles and/or physical attacks. But there's nothing that can stop the slashes of the Nobitsura Kage!! 

The RPG elements are icing on the cake, it feels somewhat similar to Borderlands. But hey if micro-managing your weapons are too much for you then you can just play this like a good-old hardcore FPS!

I was so excited to pick up the sequel to Shadow Warrior. The game had amazing fast paced classic gunplay where every weapon and shot mattered and a surprisingly intriguing story that kept up till the very end. It was lengthy with varied scenery ranging from forests, to towns, to bunkers, and snowy mountains with carefully crafted arenas and secrets scattered through. The light RPG mechanics provided a nice sense of progression that everyone seems to require in games today. The jokes while plentiful were timely and opportune enforcing Lo Wang’s character and contrasting it well with his growth with his relationship with Hoji. Hand crafted cutscenes were littered through the game beautifully retelling the tale of past and current events. The challenge was fair and the enemy variety and placement in arenas were engaging. Shadow Warrior 2 has none of these things and in fact does everything in its power to make sure it does everything worse than its predecessor.

For a frame of reference I played and beat the game on Insane difficulty and base my review and opinions on this factor. I also beat Shadow Warrior on hard and played through most of insane and beat Doom on the hardest non-permadeath difficulty.

Pros
[list]
[*]Lo Wang is back
[*]Solid gun play with a good variety of weapon types. (The majority of the weapons are however useless if not for being weak or just having weak functionality)
[*]Sword mechanics have been improved greatly. Switching between guns and swords while dashing around seamlessly is satisfying (when it works...)
[*]Well optimized while maintaining great scenery amongst the colorful elemental effects (the rain looks great!)
[*]Lengthy albeit not for the right reasons (~20+ sidequests; ~5-6 story quests)
[*]Fair selling price
[/list]

Cons
[list]
[*]Borderlands-esqe 'RPG' mechanics are the core of the game. Guns are not about using them for their range, burst potential, large clip size, etc. but rather to get the biggest damage numbers.
[*]A pointless elemental system was added. Enemies have very obvious weaknesses that you need to exploit as they are immune to certain things and vulnerable to others (ex. weak to fire, immune to ice). 
[*]Pointless loot system to augment your weapons. Generic boring random stat increases such as critical hit change, fire rate, etc. are literally exploding from enemies during the fight. You will have so much useless loot you won't know what to do with it. The choices are not engaging or meaningful and add nothing to the game. You choose elements just to counter enemy types. You stack critical hit chance and critical hit damage otherwise. This loot system has is an obvious chore and downgrade from the original.
[*]To add to the loot system there is a crafting system. The crafting system is completely random in what components you put it and what you get out. There is no reason for it to exist as there are no defined recipes for it
[*]A hub area exists and serves absolutely no purpose. Perhaps they envisioned it as a coop staging area. It detracts from the flow of the game and feels dead considering how few people are ever there.
[*]Story is a HUGE step down from the original. There is almost no story to be had to be honest. It throws everything out the window about the characters in the first game and everything is just a pointless joke after joke from Lo Wang about whoever he meets. Kamiko is not even a fraction as interesting as Hoji and it's insulting how much time she spends whining at Lo Wang while he’s fighting countless demons, robots, and gang members for HER sake. Let's be honest here. The story wouldn't be such a disappointing factor if the first game didn't set the bar so high. If Doom (2016) can have an interesting enough narrative to drive the game along in handcrafted levels, it's no excuse for a game with a really well established story to toss this facet out the window
[*]How they deal with the Nobitsura Kage and Hoji in the game is massively disappointing. It was a clear after thought and I can't even begin to fathom who thought that was a good idea.
[*]The maps are repeated so many times for both main and side quests. I feel like despite their "randomization" you can feel each section so obviously that you feel like you're in the same place over and over again. This is incredibly lazy considering the first game and how good Doom and its predecessor was at creating interesting levels
[*]Gun usage is almost entirely discouraged early on due to the lack of ammo. You will run out of ammo and be forced to use the sword
[*]Enemies are bullet sponges early on. Superior and Elites have to be simply navigated around and avoided until you get better weapons and invest in ammo upgrades. The RNG can be completely gamed if you happen to find a purple shrine to get all of your ammo back. Later in the game you'll be so powerful that everything is an afterthought. The difficulty curve of the game is not gradual line upward but a sharp slope downhill
[*]Movement mechanics frequently don't work as intended. Areas that I can hang off of one second I will crash into a wall and fall to my death the next.
[*]The game was advertised as having verticality being a huge aspect of it, but there are so many invisible walls on rooftops that prevent you from traversing how you naturally would want to get to a destination given your incredible maneuverability with dashes and double jumps.
[*]Chi powers serve no purpose on Insane. I felt it strange they placed such a strong restriction on them when they aren't that powerful to begin with due to the health pools early and lack of outgoing damage early on.
[*] (Bug) The bosses in particularly were buggy. Phase two mechanics would stick around if you die and respawn in a boss fight despite the fact that the enemies heal to full health on insane. Bosses should restart with all of your ammo at a checkpoint if they are going to get all their health back... 
[*] (Bug) The last boss was easier than the first boss of the game because it bugged out and remained on a phase where it showed its weak spot. 
[*] (Bug) After a cutscenes talking to a character I spawned outside behind a them and fell to my death.
[*]Skill points are a cheap way of taking power away from the player and creating a inflated progression system. There is no reason to have so many different sections dedicated to each element, each ammo type, etc. It's just artificial inflation with marginal gain. 
[*]The side quests had no direction or purpose. You would start with a meaningless joke exchange with a previously important character now degraded to a meaningless quest giver and then be sent off to a non-unique map for a fetch or kill quest
[*]The early transitions between areas is jarring. One second you are at a temple area and then instantly you are walking down the hall somewhere else. This happened a few times at the beginning and I genuinely thought I accidently skipped some cutscenes. It was is in fact just constructed poorly
[*]The end was an obvious cliffhanger to what I suspect will be more DLC for this game. The game seemed like it was created as a platform to provide a Borderlands coop experience and not a fast paced classic shooter.
[/list]

I could go on forever with everything that I didn't enjoy about this game. I haven't felt this disappointed with a sequel since Dragon Age 2 or Darksiders 2. Shadow Warrior 2 does in fact have enjoyable gameplay when it works. The problem is the monotony of repeat maps, low enemy variety in terms of tactics, showering unnecessary stat stick loot, lack of ammo (barring reliance on ammo shrine RNG), excessive juvenile humor (100x more so than the original), and an embarrassingly bad follow-up story make Shadow Warrior 2 one of the most disappointing, mediocre sequels. This should never ever have been an RPG shooter and whoever made this decision should be incredibly ashamed of what they did to this entry of the series.

Shadow Warrior 2 is a captivating experience packed with action, suspense, and creatures that feel like they’ve stepped straight out of mythological books. The gameplay keeps you constantly engaged, offering chaotic and satisfying combat that rarely gives you a moment to breathe.
At the same time, the game has a comedic side, mainly thanks to Lo Wang’s sense of humor. His constant jokes and comments make you laugh even while cutting down everything that stands in your way, adding a fun and unique contrast to the intense action.
The story itself can feel a bit repetitive at times, as many missions seem similar and follow the same objective. However, it still has an interesting narrative behind it. That said, I would say that Shadow Warrior 1 was more engaging overall in terms of storytelling.
In conclusion, Shadow Warrior 2 is definitely a game worth playing. It’s fun, fast-paced, and entertaining despite its flaws. I would give it a solid 7.5/10.

Shadow Warrior 2 is one of the most fun and chaotic action games I’ve played. The combat is incredibly satisfying, mixing fast-paced gunplay with brutal melee attacks. Using katanas, chainsaws, shotguns, and explosive weapons against waves of demons never gets boring. The movement also feels smooth with dashes and double jumps that make every fight intense and stylish.

What makes the game even better is the variety of weapons, upgrades, and loot. There are so many different ways to play, and customizing your loadout keeps the gameplay fresh. The co-op mode is also a big plus and makes the action even more enjoyable with friends.

The story and humor may not be for everyone, but the gameplay easily carries the experience. If you enjoy fast FPS combat, lots of gore, and nonstop action, Shadow Warrior 2 is definitely worth playing.
